newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks edge up on local support.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks edge up on local support.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed a shade higher on local buying of two highly capitalised blue chips, despite the overall trend to keep a low profile ahead of next month's local government polls, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.83 points higher at 619.07. Price declines edged out gains by 27 to 11, but John Keells Holdings rose 4.50 rupees to 180, and Hatton National Bank three rupees to 250.
"While being cautious to see if the index will fall more due to the election, some institutional investors are slowly collecting," said Dimuthu Abeysekera a trader at Allied Phillips Securities.
Retail investors, who are the most affected by wild swings in the index, were clinging to the sidelines, he said.
Turnover was 10 million rupees on 511,314 shares.
On Tuesday on the eve of a deadline for filing nominations for the March 21 polls, unknown gunmen killed a ruling People's Alliance lawmaker.
Police on Wednesday said they were searching for two opposition United National Party politicians in connection with the shooting and the UNP leader said they should report to police.
